key_insight: Time-lagged cross-correlation (TCC) identifies flow structures linked to a target observable, even when their overall contribution to the flow is small.
engineering_relevance: Observable-specific mode ranking can reveal structures associated with engineering quantities such as lift and drag without changing the underlying modal expansion.
method: Start with a fixed DMD or POD expansion, preserving spatial modes and temporal coefficients.
Rank mode groups by the mean squared norm of their cross-responses with a target observable over a lag window.
Select target-related structures rather than modes with the largest global contributions.
evidence_signal: Tests recovered three low-contribution synthetic target structures with 2.15% target-subfield reconstruction error and linked cylinder-wake and cavity modes to observable-specific dynamics.
watch_item: Benefits from lag aggregation depend on the cross-response distribution and lag-window selection; improved identification is not guaranteed.
paper_title: Extracting target-related flow structures using a time-lagged cross-correlation ranking criterion
